notes.decision: Read as ⲥⲁⲧⲡ̄ 'chosen, elect' (qualitative). The doubled -ⲧⲧ is Lycopolitan orthography. Translated 'chosen one' rather than as a proper noun (the epithet of Zarathustra in earlier kephalaia is contextually inappropriate here).
ⲕⲁⲍ = Lyc. ϩⲓⲥⲉ/ⲕⲁϩ 'suffer, be afflicted'; with negation ⲧⲙ̄- and dative -ⲛⲉⲩ. The clause expresses the protective concern of the five sons for those pleasing to them.

Translated as 'bondages' tentatively; the form may relate to ⲥⲛⲁϩ 'bond, fetter' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲥⲛⲁϩ). The pairing with ⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ 'blows' supports an affliction/restraint sense. Could alternatively be 'sufferings/afflictions' more generally.

Mani identifies himself as the Third Grieving Power, connecting this passage to the kephalaion on the Four Powers Who Grieve (cf. accumulated vocabulary ⲣ̄-ⲗⲩⲧⲏ). The first was the Mother of the Living; the second is implied earlier (probably referenced in the discussion of the Five Sons in lines 1-7); Mani is the third; the fourth would be the firmaments' weeping.
ⲟⲩⲱⲍ = Lyc. ⲟⲩⲱϩ 'add, place upon'; ⲛⲍⲏⲧⲥ̄ 'in her' (referring to the Church). 'I added (set) within her the Mind of Light.'
Read as Lyc. reflex of ⲡⲟⲩϩⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'their joining'; ϩⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'be joined, agree.' The construction ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲍⲱⲧⲏ̄ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲉⲙ = 'they did not join themselves with the right hand'. Distinct from Greek ζώνη.
Translated as 'raised up' per terminology rule on ⲧⲟⲩⲱ (preserves vertical/exposing semantics). In context of weeping, likely means 'raised up (their cry/voice) three times.'
Parsed as ⲛⲁⲩ 'see' + 3pl object suffix -ⲍⲟⲩ (Lyc. variant of ⲁⲣⲁⲩ). The construction ⲥⲉⲧⲙ̄ⲛⲁⲩⲍⲟⲩ ⲁⲣⲓⲙⲉ = 'they shall not see them weeping (again)'.

ⲉϩⲁϣⲉ qualitative 'hung, extended'; ⲁⲡⲁⲟⲉ tentatively read as a directional/spatial phrase 'at a distance' or 'far' (possibly from ⲟⲩⲉ 'be far'); ⲟⲩⲃⲏⲩ 'against them.' Translated 'hanging extended at a distance against them' to capture the cosmic looming of Darkness.
ⲛⲉⲍⲥⲉ = Lyc. ⲛⲉϩⲥⲉ 'wake up, rise up.' The future relative 'what shall rise up against them' captures the awakening of dark opposition.
Likely from a verb of hastening/rushing (possibly Lyc. for ϫⲱϣ or ϩⲱϣ 'be in haste') with reflexive 3pl. With ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'in unto him' = 'they hastened in unto him.'
